config.title: Render Props (MouseTracker)

intro.title: Render Props (MouseTracker)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a MouseTracker component that follows your cursor on the screen. You will learn the 'render props' pattern, a technique in React for sharing code between components. This involves passing a function as a prop to a component, which that component then calls to render dynamic content. You will use React state to track the mouse position and event handlers to update it. By the end, you'll understand how render props make components more reusable and flexible.
intro.usecase: The render props pattern is widely used in real-world React applications to create reusable, stateful UI logic components. For example, in interactive dashboards, a render prop component like MouseTracker can manage mouse position or hover state, enabling multiple chart or card components to react to user interaction without duplicating logic. This pattern is also common in form builders, where a render prop component handles field validation or focus state, allowing different input types to share the same behavior. By decoupling state management from presentation, render props make complex UIs like data visualizations, drag-and-drop interfaces, and dynamic filters more maintainable and scalable.

objectives: Construct a React component that tracks mouse position using state and event listeners.
Initialize and update state to reflect the current mouse coordinates.
Bind mouse event handlers to capture movement within a designated area.
Render a prop function to pass dynamic mouse data to child components.
Integrate a render prop component to control the UI output based on mouse position.
Manipulate the DOM by applying mouse coordinates to style or position elements.
Configure a reusable MouseTracker component that accepts different render functions.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules. The syntax is: import { React, useState } from 'react';
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the MouseTracker component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named MouseTracker that accepts a prop called 'render'.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name MouseTracker that takes a single parameter called 'render'.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

// Create the MouseTracker component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a MouseTracker component function that is ready to accept a 'render' prop.
successCriteria: The MouseTracker component is defined as a function or arrow function with a parameter named 'render'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'MouseTracker' and accepts a prop called 'render'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Create a function named MouseTracker that takes a 'render' parameter.

steps.title: Initialize mouse position state
steps.instruction: Inside the MouseTracker component, use useState to create a state variable called 'mousePosition' initialized to { x: 0, y: 0 }.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial object { x: 0, y: 0 } and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for coordinates
const [position, setPosition] = useState({ x: 0, y: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable ready to track mouse coordinates.
successCriteria: mousePosition state is declared using useState with initial value { x: 0, y: 0 }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the state to track mouse position.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the correct initial object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've declared the state variable with useState inside the component.

steps.title: Define the mouse move handler
steps.instruction: Inside the MouseTracker component, define a function named handleMouseMove that takes an event parameter and updates the mousePosition state with the event's clientX and clientY properties.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives the event object and calls setMousePosition with an object containing x and y coordinates from the event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleMouseMove function that updates state when called with mouse event data.
successCriteria: A handleMouseMove function is defined that calls setMousePosition with an object containing x and y values from event.clientX and event.clientY.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and calls setMousePosition with an object containing both x and y coordinates from the event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleMouseMove function should update the mousePosition state with coordinates from the mouse event.

steps.title: Add mouse event listener on mount
steps.instruction: Inside the MouseTracker component, add a useEffect hook to set up a 'mousemove' event listener on the window when the component mounts. The event listener should call the handleMouseMove function.
steps.hint: Use useEffect with an empty dependency array to run code only on mount. Inside the effect, add an event listener to the window for 'mousemove' events, passing handleMouseMove as the callback. Don't forget to return a cleanup function that removes the event listener.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now track mouse movement by listening to 'mousemove' events when it mounts.
successCriteria: A useEffect hook is added with an empty dependency array that adds a 'mousemove' event listener to the window, calling handleMouseMove, and includes a cleanup function to remove the listener.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect has an empty dependency array, adds the event listener correctly, and includes a cleanup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The event listener isn't set up correctly. Remember to use useEffect with an empty dependency array to add the 'mousemove' listener to the window, and include a cleanup function.

steps.title: Remove mouse event listener on unmount
steps.instruction: Add a cleanup function to remove the 'mousemove' event listener when the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Return a cleanup function from the useEffect that removes the event listener using removeEventListener.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will clean up the event listener when it unmounts, preventing memory leaks.
successCriteria: A cleanup function is returned from useEffect that calls removeEventListener with 'mousemove' and handleMouseMove.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the cleanup function calls removeEventListener with the correct event and handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function is missing or incorrect. Remember to return a function from useEffect that removes the event listener.

steps.title: Return the render prop call
steps.instruction: Inside your MouseTracker component, return the result of calling the 'render' prop function with the current mousePosition state.
steps.hint: The render prop is passed as a prop to MouseTracker. Call it like a function and pass mousePosition as an argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseTracker component now returns the result of calling the render prop with mousePosition, enabling the render props pattern.
successCriteria: The component returns render(mousePosition) where render is a prop function and mousePosition is the state object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling the render prop function and passing mousePosition as an argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return the result of calling the render prop with mousePosition. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Create the DisplayMouse component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DisplayMouse that returns MouseTracker with a render prop.
steps.hint: Define a new component that calls MouseTracker and passes a function as its render prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new DisplayMouse component is defined that will use MouseTracker with a render prop.
successCriteria: DisplayMouse component is created and returns MouseTracker with a render prop function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating DisplayMouse, but make sure it returns MouseTracker with a render prop function.
steps.feedbackWrong: DisplayMouse component is not properly defined or doesn't return MouseTracker with a render prop.

steps.title: Implement the render prop function
steps.instruction: In the DisplayMouse component, pass a function to MouseTracker's render prop that returns JSX displaying the mouse coordinates.
steps.hint: The function should take the mousePosition object as an argument and return JSX that shows the x and y values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DisplayMouse component will call MouseTracker with a render prop function that displays the mouse position.
successCriteria: DisplayMouse passes a function to MouseTracker that returns JSX showing the x and y coordinates from mousePosition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function takes mousePosition as an argument and returns JSX that shows both x and y values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The render prop function isn't implemented correctly. It should take mousePosition and return JSX displaying the coordinates.

steps.title: Export and use the components
steps.instruction: Export both MouseTracker and DisplayMouse components,
steps.hint: Use named exports for both components, then make sure your main component returns the DisplayMouse component.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both components are exported and DisplayMouse is rendered in the app.
successCriteria: MouseTracker and DisplayMouse are exported, and the main component returns DisplayMouse.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but make sure to export both MouseTracker and DisplayMouse, and render DisplayMouse in your main component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step isn't complete. You need to export both MouseTracker and DisplayMouse, then render DisplayMouse in your app.
